verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is visible from Florida, Orlando, and parts of southern Georgia shortly after liftoff.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'If you are in Florida or Georgia...'; R3: 'visible for most of Florida to parts of Georgia... east Orlando'; R4: 'Orlando... southern Georgia'; R6: 'most of Florida and southeastern Georgia'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm visibility from Florida (including Orlando) and southern Georgia shortly after liftoff.

verifications.claim: Major broadcast options for the Artemis II launch include NASA+ (desktop and mobile app), NASA's YouTube Channel, Amazon Prime Video, and local news channels.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA YouTube page... NASA+ mobile app... Amazon Prime Video... Local TV channels CBS, ABC, NBC, and Fox News'; R3: 'NASA+ on desktop... YouTube... Prime Video'; R5: 'NASA+... YouTube... Amazon Prime'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly list these exact broadcast options.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II rocket will likely be visible for about 70 seconds before exiting the immediate lower atmosphere.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: visibility up to 'Launch + 70 seconds'; R4: 'lost from view just 70 seconds after launch... altitude of over 40,000 feet'; R6: '10 seconds to 70 seconds after liftoff'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm ~70 seconds visibility until exiting lower atmosphere/atmosphere layers.

verifications.claim: NASA’s YouTube and NASA+ provide continuous coverage of the Artemis II launch, starting early on launch day.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA live stream has been active since 7:45 a.m.... YouTube... NASA+'; R2: '24/7 coverage will continue on NASA’s YouTube channel'; R5: 'YouTube ... begins ... 7:45 a.m. ... continuously... NASA+ ... beginning at 12:50 p.m.'
verifications.reasoning: YouTube provides continuous from early (7:45am); NASA+ starts later (12:50pm) but provides coverage; claim slightly broadens 'continuous starting early' for both.
